name: chainedr_external_bytecode_v1
description: External bytecode benchmark — runtime bytecode fetched live from mainnet via eth_getCode for verified deployed contracts. None of these bytes were authored by the ChainEDR maintainers. Each label records what `detect_bytecode_aa7702()` fires on the runtime + the maintainer triage verdict + the on-chain source so a reviewer can re-fetch.
policy: Verdicts are: TP (real signal worth surfacing), ARCH (architecture advisory the bytecode-level rule is meant to surface — typically infrastructure that legitimately uses the flagged opcode), FP (false positive needing a future detector fix), or N/A (clean bytecode, no AA7702-* finding expected).

samples.rationale: Known 7702 delegator implementation (1,511 live delegations per Path-A hunt). Compact 789-byte runtime; the implementation has no tx.origin / extcodesize / delegatecall patterns at the opcode level.

ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.7. As infrastructure, EntryPoint legitimately uses EXTCODESIZE (target validation), DELEGATECALL (account-bound execution), and SELFDESTRUCT machinery. At the source level the AA infrastructure filter excludes these. The bytecode-mode detector cannot recover that file-level context — it surfaces the raw opcodes as architecture advisories a reviewer should manually classify.

Ithaca Account on mainnet. The bytecode contains code.length / extcodehash checks (likely 1271 routing) and delegatecall (executor path). At the source level (P33) we already flagged Ithaca with AA7702-012 + AA7702-013 advisories — the bytecode-level fires are consistent: real architecture surface, not exploits.

Uniswap Permit2 deployed on mainnet. AA7702-010 fired at the SOURCE level (signature replay surface), but the opcode patterns AA7702-001 / 002 / 006 / 015 do not appear. Source-mode is the right detector for this class; bytecode-mode complementing it correctly stays silent.
